correctness.rationale: The first coordinate forces any primitive return to interchange x and y, so the two scalar interchange equations are necessary and sufficient. Independently translating X=x+c and Y=y+c, the equations become X(Y²−2cY+L)=N and Y(X²−2cX+L)=N. Their difference forces XY=L off the diagonal; then each reduces to L(X+Y−2c)=N. For L≠0 the unordered distinct pair is therefore determined by one monic quadratic, giving exactly the asserted discriminant and cusp; equality gives a fixed point, not a cycle. For L=0 the conditions instead give N=0 and the union of the two axes in translated variables, with the common origin excluded. Multiplication of the two Jacobians gives the recorded determinant and trace and 1−T+D=LΔ. This yields the strict Schur inequalities and a real multiplier above one if L<0. On the sink slice, D<1 iff −4/3<S<0, Δ>0 iff S<−2−sqrt(2) or S>−2+sqrt(2), and 1+T+D>0 everywhere. Their intersection gives the stated interval; the neutral and coalescence endpoints are not sinks. Direct differentiation on the resonant slice gives a triangular return matrix with tangent multiplier 1 and normal multiplier t², not individual-cycle attraction.
correctness.replay: Expand the translated orbit-equation difference (X−Y)(L−XY) and sum (X+Y)(XY+L)−4cXY−2N. An independent symbolic check verified both and 1−T+D=LΔ upon substituting P=L−c²−cS. The interval then follows by exact signs of the slice polynomials, not parameter sampling. The packaged verify.py was inspected, not executed.
residual_risks: The stability criterion is for a hyperbolic/exponentially attracting period-two orbit. No nonlinear stability conclusion is obtained at unit multipliers. The resonant normal statements are pointwise, away from the neutral and collapsed cases.
